reflection: Round 1, no notebook yet. With no history, improve and partner factors are built from the most useful existing factors (AAPL 10d/20d volatility, MSFT 1d return, NVDA 5d return). I will test mean-reversion, volatility regime and peer-lead ideas and learn which years and models respond.

factors.name: aapl_vol_ratio_5_20
factors.hypothesis: Raw volatility level depends on the regime and differs across years; the short/long ratio captures vol expansion or contraction, which is scale-free and more stable across years.

factors.name: msft_return_zscore_20d
factors.hypothesis: MSFT's raw 1d return is scaled differently in high- and low-vol years; standardizing it makes the signal comparable across regimes.

factors.name: aapl_close_position_in_range
factors.hypothesis: Where the close sits in the day's range shows end-of-day buying or selling pressure, which may continue or revert next day.

factors.name: qqq_vol_ratio_5_20
factors.hypothesis: Rising short-term tech-market volatility relative to its norm signals stress, after which rebounds in AAPL are more likely.

factors.name: aapl_overnight_gap
factors.hypothesis: Apple's overnight gap relative to QQQ's gap complements the volatility state by showing idiosyncratic sentiment, which tends to revert intraday and next day.

factors.name: peer_dispersion_5d
factors.hypothesis: When NVDA and MSFT disagree over 5 days, tech leadership is unstable; this conditions how the NVDA 5d momentum feeds into AAPL.
